basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Et statuam pactum meum inter me et te, et inter semen tuum post te in generationibus suis'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Et statuam pactum meum inter me et te, et inter semen tuum post te in generationibus suis foedere sempiterno; ut sim Deus tuus et seminis tui post te. Vetus translatio habet: Et statuam testamentum meum. Notandum autem quod ubicunque in Graeco legimus testamentum, ibi in Hebraeo sermone sit foedus, sive pactum, id est, berith. Non est autem mirandum quare testamentum sive pactum Dei sit cum Abraham et semine ejus foedere sempiterno, ut sit Deus eorum: quia nimirum hoc foedus, et toto tempore vitae hujus sine ulla intermissione in generationibus electorum sese ex ordine sequentium servabitur, et in futuro saeculo sine ullo fine celebrabitur.
